accessNotes: The official chart-guide URL on design-system.economist.com now returns the Gatsby site shell (HTML) instead of the PDF and the Wayback Machine was offline, so the identical 25-page 'The Economist visual styleguide, Version 1.2, Updated 4 May 2017' PDF was read from a mirror (sa.ipaa.org.au). The map style guide PDF (v1.2, 5 May 2017, 12 pages) downloaded directly from the official URL. Text extracted with pypdf; key pages rendered with Ghostscript and inspected visually. Print values are in points/CMYK; web values are given as hex. Pixel sizes below are derived from the guide's statement that web charts are built at print width and exported at 179.22% (332pt -> 595px).
summary: Editorial newsmagazine charts: compact, information-dense, condensed sans-serif (Econ Sans Cnd) with a short bold headline that is a pun or finding, a regular-weight subtitle stating measure and units, and a signature red tab/red rule at top-left. Value axis labels sit on the right, gridlines are horizontal only, and the source line sits bottom-left in light grey. Print charts sit on a pale blue-grey background; the 2017 web redesign moved to a white background with a thin red line across the top.

colors.categoricalNotes: Web 'MAIN' palette as listed on the web palette page: RED #DB444B, BLUE #006BA2, CYAN #3EBCD2, GREEN #379A8B, YELLOW #EBB434, OLIVE #B4BA39, PURPLE #9A607F, GOLD #D1B07C, plus GREY #758D99. The ordered list above maps the guide's bar/line 'COLOUR ORDER 1-6' swatches (dark blue, light blue/cyan, yellow-gold, teal-green, dark red, mauve; shown in print CMYK) onto the nearest web MAIN hexes - the mapping is an inference from swatch appearance. Scatter/bubble charts use a different order: 1 cyan, 2 dark red, 3 yellow, 4 dark blue, 5 teal, 6 mauve. 'Ilex will plot up to 6 colours but any more than 4 categories is probably too many and you should have a rethink.' Use grey for 'other'/'don't know'. Where categories are chronological use a light-to-dark scale of one hue; if categories form meaningful groups use colour (shades of one hue) to reinforce that. Differentiate positive/negative by colour only where meaningful (e.g. exports blue / imports red). A 'high contrast alternatives' set exists for lines.
colors.notes: ECON RED #E3120B (brand red used for the tab/top rule, not as a data colour - data red is #DB444B). BLACK #0C0C0C. TEXT #3F5661. BOXES/NAV #E9EDF0, #B7C6CF, #758D99. 'EQUAL LIGHTNESS COLOUR SCALES' (6 steps, dark->light) per hue: RED A81829 C7303C E64E53 FF6B6C FF8785 FFA39F; BLUE 00588D 1270A8 3D89C3 5DA4DF 7BBFFC 98DAFF; CYAN 005F73 00788D 0092A7 25ADC2 4EC8DE 6FE4FB; GREEN 005F52 00786B 2E9284 4DAD9E 69C9B9 86E5D4; YELLOW 714C00 8D6300 AA7C00 C89608 E7B030 FFCB4D; OLIVE 4C5900 667100 818A00 9DA521 BAC03F D7DB5A; PURPLE 78405F 925977 AD7291 C98CAC E6A6C7 FFC2E3; GOLD 674E1F 826636 9D7F4E B99966 D5B480 F2CF9A; GREY 3F5661 576E79 6F8793 89A2AE A4BDC9 BFD8E5. The diverging list above is assembled from the BLUE and RED scales (not a guide-specified diverging ramp). Print palette (CMYK): ECON RED C0 M100 Y100 K0; print background C7.5 K5 (pale blue-grey); grid lines/grey box/grey text/number box are listed as cyan+black tints (e.g. number box c22.5 k15, grey c15 k10). Old design used the print background; the 'new design' web chart has a white background, source text 75% black. Web gridline colour is not given as hex; rendered examples show light blue-grey horizontal rules. Zero baseline is black ('use black for zero baseline only'); in the scatter and +/- bar examples a red horizontal line marks zero.

typography.family: Econ Sans Cnd (condensed) with Econ Sans bold for headlines

subtitle.weight: regular (Econ Sans Cnd regular 8/9.5pt); sub-subtitle/units line light 7.5/9pt

axisTitle.placement: y-axis: omitted, units go in subtitle; x-axis title (when needed) centred below tick labels in cnd regular 7pt

dataLabel.weight: Econ Sans Cnd light/regular 7-7.5pt; legend labels cnd light 7.5/9pt

source.style: Econ Sans Cnd light 6.5pt, 75% black, starts 'Source:' or 'Sources:'

typography.notes: Print sizes in pt (web px = pt x 1.7922): headline Econ Sans bold 9.5/11pt; subtitle Econ Sans Cnd regular 8/9.5; sub-subtitle/legend heading Econ Sans Cnd medium 7.5/9; legend items cnd light 7.5/9; y tick labels cnd light 7pt; x axis label cnd reg 7/7.5; source cnd light 6.5pt 75k. Leader-block (small) charts: bold 8pt / cnd reg 7pt / light 6pt. Espresso charts: title Econ Sans Cnd bold 8pt. Econ Sans Cnd light used for most chart labelling; medium for panel headings/coloured text; bold for chart headlines and oversize numbers. Use Econ Sans Cnd Regular (not light) for coloured y-axis labels on double-scale charts. Footnote symbols order: * † ‡ § ** †† ‡‡ §§. Years abbreviated after the first: '1985 90 95 2000 05 10 16'. Highlight labels / forecast labels: Econ Sans Cnd light 6.5pt UPPERCASE. Maps: country names Econ Sans Cnd bold 9pt tracked to 400, uppercase.

structure.gridlines: Horizontal only, light blue-grey, 0.5pt thick (print); no vertical gridlines on time-series. Horizontal bar charts use vertical gridlines from the top value axis.
structure.axisLine: x-axis baseline drawn in black (0.4pt) and ends at the last tick mark; no y-axis line. Axis lines can be broken on connected scatters to avoid obscuring labels.
structure.ticks: x-axis tick marks hang below the baseline, 0.4pt thick, with heights 5 (major) / 3 / 2 (minor). No y ticks - gridlines extend under the labels.
structure.zeroLine: Zero baseline in black ('use black for zero baseline only'); in +/- bar and scatter examples zero is drawn as a red line.
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted - units are given in the subtitle (e.g. 'Ten-year government-bond yields, %'); a separate smaller second line can hold units/date
structure.unitPlacement: In the subtitle after a comma ('..., %', '$bn', '2015=100'); y tick labels are bare numbers sitting just above the gridlines at the right edge.
structure.frame: No border. Signature red tab (15pt wide x 5pt tall rectangle) at top-left above the headline; web charts also have a thin red rule across the full chart width at the top.
structure.background: Web (2017 new design): white. Print: pale blue-grey (C7.5 K5) panel, 6pt internal margins.
structure.notes: Standard print chart 160pt (1 column) wide, 165pt typical height; vertical rhythm 5 (tab) /17 (title) /11 (subtitle) /15 (legend) /10 ... /10 (x labels) /10 (axis title) /10 (source). Web charts built at 332pt and exported at 179.22% to 595px; 1-column 160pt -> 290px. Panel charts: 24pt spacer between panels, panels marked with a marker. Broken-scale symbol: black 0.4pt zig-zag, 6pt wide, centred between baseline and first y tick; never break bar/column scales - use a thermometer chart instead.

legend.placement: top, left-aligned under the subtitle (web 2-column chart: top-right, in line with title)
legend.directLabels: Preferred where possible for lines (labels in series colour next to the line) and for scatter outliers; pies use linking lines or small colour blocks when crowded; maps label directly with a highlight box instead of a key when one variable is shown.
legend.title: Optional legend heading in Econ Sans Cnd medium 7.5pt (e.g. 'Period beginning:', 'Forecasts made in:')
legend.swatchShape: short thick line for line charts; small rectangle/square for bars; circle for scatter categories
legend.notes: Legend items in a row (or 2-column grid) in cnd light 7.5/9.

marks.bars: Flat filled bars, no outlines, no rounded corners; horizontal bars common for categories with labels on the left and value axis on top; narrow gaps. Stacked bars: for few categories, remove ticks and label each segment value. Do not break the scale on bars - use thermometer (dot/line) instead.
marks.lines: Solid, roughly 1pt (thick relative to 0.5pt gridlines), no point markers; up to ~4-6 colours. Trend lines 1px dashed 3px,1px. Index charts: 5pt black circle on index point, 0.5pt red line on index line.
marks.areas: Stacked areas in the standard colour order; alternative light-to-dark single-hue scheme for chronological categories.
marks.points: Standard dot 4px, 50% opacity; highlight dot 4px, 100% opacity; category/bubble dot 0.3px stroke with 50% opacity fill.
marks.pies: 'Use with caution. Should probably be abandoned in favour of stacked bar if over 4 categories.' Doughnut with total in the centre; labels with linking lines or keyed colour blocks.
marks.notes: Thermometer (dot-range) charts with dot terminals as an alternative when lines are unclear. Blob-heads: secondary value shown as bubbles or number boxes (fill c22.5 k15, 12pt high, 6pt padding).

labels.dataLabels: Used on stacked bars (inside segments) and pies; number boxes fill c22.5 k15; bubbles carry numbers inside if they fit, otherwise outside right-aligned. Leader-block charts emphasise the overall message over individual values.
labels.numberFormat: Bare numbers on axis, units in subtitle ('$bn', '%', '’000', '$trn'); negative values with minus sign; thousands with comma (e.g. 173,070).
labels.dates: Years abbreviated to two digits after the first and at century change: '1985 90 95 2000 05 10 16'; months as single initials 'J F M A M J J A S O N D' with year beneath.
labels.notes: Footnotes use symbols * † ‡ § in that order and are explained right-aligned on the source line.

furniture.title: Headline is a short witty phrase ('Where Tokyo leads', 'Mutti's malaise') in Econ Sans bold; subtitle states what is measured, geography and units ('Ten-year government-bond yields, %'). 'Where possible, put units and date information on a second line at smaller font size.' Subtitle should summarise the chart, saving specific units for axis labels on scatters.
furniture.source: Required. Bottom-left, Econ Sans Cnd light 6.5pt, 75% black: 'Source: Thomson Reuters' or 'Sources: A; B; The Economist'. Footnote explanations ('*Estimate') right-aligned on the same line.
furniture.logo: No logo on charts; brand presence is the red tab (ECON RED #E3120B) at top-left and, on web, the red top rule.
furniture.other: Red tab 15pt x 5pt top-left; web: thin red line spanning the full width at the top. Number boxes (Econ Sans bold 7.5pt, c22.5/k15, 10pt square) top-right for charts referenced in text. Highlight panels: shaded vertical bands - grey c15 k10 with 'FORECAST' label (light 6.5pt uppercase) for secondary info; red 30% tint (c10 m70 y50) for highlights central to the message.

annotations: Thin 0.5pt stroke leader lines with small arrowheads ('arrow 21') from label to point; label text Econ Sans Cnd light 7/7pt. Event markers: thin vertical red lines from the x-axis with small red labels. If only 1 or 2 points are key, use colour/medium font. Timelines: thin alternating-colour bars mark periods; grey labels when colour categorises data; dotted lines for labels on bar charts. Reference lines (e.g. '2013 average 80.5') dashed with bold label.
layout: Fixed column widths: print 1 column 160pt (web 290px), 2 column 332pt (web 595px), 3 column 504pt; leader/WTW 117pt x 83.5pt fixed height (web 290px); espresso 160pt with fixed depth and 40pt blank spacer. Web charts built at print size and exported at 179.22%. 6pt side margins in print; new web design has no margins. Panel charts: 24pt spacer between panels. Timelines: on mobile rotate vertically or compress and number labels.
accessibility: Not explicitly addressed. Equal-lightness colour scales are provided; advice to avoid more than 4 categories and to highlight the most significant part of the story when colours become hard to distinguish.

discouraged: double-scale charts with misaligned zeros, broken scales or forced correlation
chartTypes.notes: Double scales allowed if zero lines align; colour the y-axis labels to match their series (Econ Sans Cnd Regular). Maps: white background with red line for locator maps; Robinson for world, Lambert for continents, Mercator for zoomed-in; national borders 0.75pt white, regional borders 0.5pt dashed white, coastline 0.5pt.

distinctiveRules.rule: Red tab (ECON RED #E3120B, ~15pt x 5pt) at the top-left corner of every chart, above the headline; web charts add a thin red rule across the full chart width at the top.
distinctiveRules.quote: Dimensions page shows red block 15 wide x 5 high; 'What's changed' lists 'rotated tag'; web example has red line along top

distinctiveRules.rule: Value (y) axis labels are on the right-hand side, right-aligned at the chart edge, sitting just above their gridline; no y-axis line and no y tick marks.
distinctiveRules.quote: Standard print/web examples: 'cnd light 7pt' tick labels at right end of gridlines

distinctiveRules.rule: Only horizontal gridlines (0.5pt light blue-grey); x-axis baseline in black 0.4pt that ends at the last tick mark, with tick marks hanging below (heights 5/3/2pt).
distinctiveRules.quote: TICKMARKS 0.5pt thickness / 0.4pt thickness, height 5 3 2; 'x axis baseline ends at last tick mark'

distinctiveRules.rule: No y-axis title: headline (bold) + subtitle (regular) stating measure and units ('Ten-year government-bond yields, %'), units/date on a second smaller line.
distinctiveRules.quote: Where possible, put units and date information on a second line at smaller font size

distinctiveRules.rule: Typography in Econ Sans: headline bold 9.5/11pt, subtitle condensed regular 8/9.5pt, labels condensed light 7-7.5pt, source condensed light 6.5pt at 75% black (web = pt x 1.79).
distinctiveRules.quote: Econ sans bold 9.5/11pt; Econ sans cnd regular 8/9.5; Source: cnd light 6.5pt 75k

distinctiveRules.rule: Source line bottom-left beginning 'Source:'/'Sources:', with footnote explanations (*, †, ‡) right-aligned on the same line.
distinctiveRules.quote: Sources: International Olympic Committee; Sports Reference; The Economist   *Unified team of ex-Soviet republics

distinctiveRules.rule: Web charts on white background with no margins; print charts on pale blue-grey (C7.5 K5) panel.
distinctiveRules.quote: NEW DESIGN: White background ... No margins ... Source text 75% black ... New colour palette ... New typeface

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend sits at the top, left-aligned under the subtitle (or top-right on wide web charts), with short line or square swatches; direct labels preferred for lines.
distinctiveRules.quote: Standard print/web examples: legend row under subtitle 'cnd light 7.5/9'

distinctiveRules.rule: Series colour order starts with dark blue (#006BA2) then light blue/cyan (#3EBCD2), then gold, teal, dark red, mauve; use grey for 'other'; more than 4 categories is 'probably too many'.
distinctiveRules.quote: Ilex will plot up to 6 colours but any more than 4 categories is probably too many ... Use grey for 'other' / 'dont know'

distinctiveRules.rule: Chronological categories use a light-to-dark single-hue scale (equal-lightness scales provided per hue).
distinctiveRules.quote: Where categories are chronological, use light-to-dark scale

distinctiveRules.rule: Years abbreviated to two digits after the first label and at century change (1985 90 95 2000 05 10 16).
Forecast/estimate periods shown as a grey shaded vertical band labelled 'FORECAST' in light 6.5pt uppercase; message-critical periods as a 30% red-tint band.
distinctiveRules.quote: For secondary information, like forecast or estimate, use neutral style ... For highlights that are central to the message of the chart, use colour

distinctiveRules.rule: Scatter dots 4px at 50% opacity; highlight dots 100% opacity; bubbles 0.3px stroke with 50% fill; trend lines 1px dashed 3,1.
distinctiveRules.quote: Standard dot 4px width 50% opacity ... trend lines 1px stroke dashed 3px, 1px

distinctiveRules.rule: Pie/doughnut only with caution - switch to stacked bar above 4 categories; never break the scale on bar charts (use a thermometer chart).
distinctiveRules.quote: Should probably be abandoned in favour of stacked bar if over 4 categories ... DON'T BREAK SCALE ON BAR/COLUMN CHARTS

distinctiveRules.rule: Locator maps: red tab top-left, white national borders 0.75pt, dashed white regional borders, country names in spaced uppercase condensed bold, inset globe locator box.
distinctiveRules.quote: 0.75pt / solid / WHITE national border; 0.5pt / dashed 3pt,1pt / WHITE regional border; Econ sans cnd bold 9pt (tracked to 400)

referenceImages.describes: Standard web chart 'National anthem monopolies' (stacked columns). White background; thin red line across the entire top edge with a short thicker red tab at top-left. Headline bold dark sans, left-aligned; subtitle regular below ('Number of “medal sweeps” by country'). Legend at top-right in a 2x2 grid with small square swatches: dark blue (United States), salmon red (Soviet Union), cyan (East Germany), light blue-grey (Other). Horizontal light blue-grey gridlines only; y tick labels (0-12) on the right edge just above each gridline; no y-axis line; x-axis baseline black with labels '1948 52 56 ... 2000 04 08 12 16'. Bars flat, no outlines, moderately narrow gaps. Source line bottom-left in light grey condensed ('Sources: ...; The Economist' with The Economist in italic); footnote '*Unified team of ex-Soviet republics' right-aligned on the same line.

Standard print chart spec 'Where Tokyo leads' with measured dimensions: pale blue-grey background panel, red tab top-left (15x5pt), bold headline 9.5/11pt, condensed subtitle 8/9.5, legend heading medium 7.5/9 ('Period beginning:'), legend items light 7.5/9 with short thick line swatches in dark blue and cyan. Two lines, ~1pt thick, no markers. Horizontal grey gridlines, y labels right-aligned at the right edge above the lines; x-axis black baseline with hanging ticks of three heights (5/3/2) and labels '1 5 10 13', axis title 'Years since start' centred below; 'Source: Thomson Reuters' bottom-left in tiny light grey.

Bar/column examples on blue-grey panels, each with red tab, bold headline and subtitle. Horizontal bars have category labels left, value axis labels across the top, thin vertical gridlines; single-series in dark blue with one highlighted bar in cyan. COLOUR ORDER swatches 1-6: dark blue, cyan, sand/gold, teal, dark red, mauve. Diverging +/- bar charts show a red zero line; imports/exports chart uses blue above and red below zero. Chronological categories shown as light-to-dark blues/teals.

Miscellaneous styles: number box (light blue square with white bold numeral) at top-right of chart; grey shaded 'FORECAST' band with uppercase light label; pink 30% red-tint highlight bands labelled 'Euro Crisis'/'Migrant Crisis' in red; event labels with thin red vertical leader lines and small arrowheads; index chart with black dot on index point and thin red index line; broken-scale zig-zag symbol between baseline and first tick.

Web chart palette page: ECON RED E3120B, BLACK 0C0C0C, BOXES/NAV E9EDF0/B7C6CF/758D99, TEXT 3F5661; MAIN row RED DB444B, BLUE 006BA2, CYAN 3EBCD2, GREEN 379A8B, YELLOW EBB434, OLIVE B4BA39, PURPLE 9A607F, GOLD D1B07C, GREY 758D99; six-step equal-lightness scales for each hue.

Locator map examples: each with red tab top-left; land in warm light grey, focus countries in muted teal/green, highlight regions in salmon/orange; sea pale blue with italic blue water labels; country names in widely letter-spaced uppercase; white borders; small inset globe/locator boxes in corners; scale bar bottom; data-overlay map keys in a white box at bottom with 'Source:' line.
